== Research note ==
The mother of Richard's daughter Mary Busby Pike is given as "Margaret ''White''" in her 1891 Scottish death record.<ref>See sources for {{FamilySearch|M73B-9H8}} (Mary Busby Pike)</ref> That Richard was indeed Mary's father is confirmed by newspaper notices for Mary's 1890 second marriage, describing her as "Mary Beatrice [''sic''], widow of Charles A Gray, LRCP &c Glasgow, and daughter of the late Richard Pike, Esq., of Beechgrove, County Tyrone".

Further investigation would be useful to clarify whether Margaret "White" should be taken to be the same as Margaret McKeighan; or whether she was Richard's second wife; or whether it was some other Richard who married Margaret McKeighan in 1842.

== Research Notes ==
=== Richard Pike’s daughter’s marriage, 1864 ===

A notice states that Benjamin Glasgow of Drapersfield, Cookstown, married Wilhelmina, eldest daughter of Richard Pike, Esq., of Beechgrove, Dungannon, at Dungannon on 16 February 1864.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/387828785/ Belfast News-Letter, 18 February 1864, p.2].</ref>

The distinctive Wilhelmina name, Richard father and Beechgrove/Dungannon location strongly fit the existing Richard–Wilhelmina family. The Quaker birth transcription gives Wilhelmina born at Torren Hill on 11 November 1842 to Richard and Margaret. The newspaper names her father independently; the underlying Quaker image has not been newly inspected.
